title: Sell Mineral Rights in Northport, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Northport, AL | Tuscaloosa County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Northport, AL across the river from Tuscaloosa? Get a title-researched offer with no pressure to sign anything.
heroLead: Northport sits across the Black Warrior River from Tuscaloosa, close enough to the productive coalbed methane fields around Brookwood and Cedar Cove that families here often hold interests without ever having set foot on the actual leased tract.
intro: A lot of Northport residents own mineral interests tied to rural land elsewhere in Tuscaloosa County — a grandparent's farm out toward Brookwood, or acreage that's been in the family since before the town grew into what it is today. Because the interest and the family's current address don't match, these often sit unmanaged for years, with royalty checks going to an old address or a relative who's since passed, and nobody quite sure who's supposed to be handling it now.

sections.heading: When the Land and the Family Have Drifted Apart
paragraphs: If your family moved into Northport generations ago but still owns minerals out toward the rural parts of the county, the first step is simply confirming the interest is still correctly recorded in your name or your family's name. We check the Tuscaloosa County record and identify exactly what's owned before we discuss what it might be worth.

sections.heading: Redirecting a Royalty Check That's Gone Astray
paragraphs: It's common for royalty payments to stop reaching the right person after a move, a death, or a name change that was never reported to the operator. If that's happened with your family's interest, we can often help identify where the checks have been going and what needs to be corrected before a sale, or as part of one.

faqs.question: We're not sure our address is still on file with the operator. How do we check?
faqs.answer: We can help identify where payments have been going and what's on record with the operator, as part of confirming your interest before we make an offer.

faqs.question: The land itself is out near Brookwood, not Northport. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: No — we research wherever the tract actually sits in Tuscaloosa County, regardless of where your family lives today.

faqs.question: Our checks stopped years ago after a relative passed away. What now?
faqs.answer: That's usually a probate issue — the interest needs to pass to the current heirs of record before payments resume. We'll walk you through what's needed.

faqs.question: Is it worth pursuing an interest we know very little about?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Send us whatever fragment of information you have — an old check stub, a probate reference, even a family name — and we'll research it from there.
